name: Baja California
summary_text: No criminalisation of trans presence. The state congress created an administrative legal gender recognition procedure in a 2022 Civil Code reform; after the Supreme Court struck down its adults-only limit in June 2023, a new reform passed in 2024 extended recognition to children and adolescents. In May 2022 the congress also added a penal-code chapter "Crimes against Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression". The counterweight is Tijuana: the state attorney general publicly warned of a serial killer of women in prostitution there (at least 3 victims; suspect arrested July 2023 after an Interpol notice and FBI cooperation), only 22 of 278 killed women in the state were classed as feminicides, and a 2021 burning of a trans woman's body in her Tijuana home is recorded within that pattern. Mixed: protective law, under-counted lethal risk concentrated in one border city.

sources.title: Trans Rights in Mexico: Progress and Challenges | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch state-by-state tracker on legal gender recognition in Mexico (March 2025), covering which of the 32 states have legislated an administrative procedure and the Supreme Court rulings that drove expansion. For Baja California: 2022 Civil Code reform created an administrative legal gender recognition procedure for adults; the Supreme Court invalidated its 18-years requirement in June 2023; a 2024 reform followed.

sources.title: “I Just Want to Contribute to Society”: The Need for Legal Gender Recognition in Tabasco, Mexico | HRW
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch report 'I Just Want to Contribute to Society' (6 March 2024) on Tabasco: no legal gender recognition procedure there exposes trans people to institutional mistreatment - the August 2023 killing of activist Karina Gomez remained unsolved, hate-motivation provisions are absent from Tabasco's criminal code, and healthcare staff routinely out patients by calling legal names. Baseline for how a non-reforming state behaves.

sources.title: Transfemicide becomes a crime in a ‘watershed’ moment for Mexico City | Transgender | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: Guardian report (24 July 2024) on Mexico City making transfemicide a crime with sentences up to 70 years (the 'Paola Buenrostro law', approved 18 July 2024), in one of Latin America's deadliest settings for trans people; over 95% of homicides nationally went unpunished in 2022.
